title: 2 Samuel Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on 2 Samuel 9: David shows kindness to Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, for Jonathan's sake.

questions.text: For whose sake did David want to show kindness to someone of Saul's house?
questions.explanation: David asked whether anyone was left of Saul's house, that he might show him kindness for Jonathan's sake.

questions.text: What was the name of the servant of Saul's house who was called to David?
questions.explanation: There was of Saul's house a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David.
Ziba said he was in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.

answers.text: In the king's palace in Jerusalem
In the house of Machir in Lo Debar

questions.text: What did Mephibosheth do when he came to David?
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth came to David, fell on his face, and showed respect.

answers.text: He fell on his face and showed respect
He ran away from David in fear
He asked for his father's crown
He brought David a costly gift

questions.text: What did David promise to restore to Mephibosheth?
questions.explanation: David said, "I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father."

answers.text: All the land of Saul his father
A city of his own choosing

questions.text: Where did David say Mephibosheth would eat bread continually?
questions.explanation: David said, "You will eat bread at my table continually."

questions.text: How did Mephibosheth describe himself to David?
questions.explanation: He bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?"

answers.text: As a worm in the dust

questions.text: How many sons and servants did Ziba have?
questions.explanation: Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

questions.text: What was the name of Mephibosheth's young son?
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica.

questions.text: In which city did Mephibosheth live?
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king's table.
